BiblicalUsage: A cleft of the rock is a hollowed-out hiding place, and it is where God puts Moses when His glory passes by. The same word covers the clefts where men hide from the fear of the LORD when He rises to shake the earth — the rock shelters one man and swallows the fear of the rest.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the cleft is the picture of my safety: I cannot stand in the open before God's glory, but He Himself sets me in the rock.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
